patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenCart and Squarespace share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose OpenCart only if your buying job matches “GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by” rather than Squarespace's shape. Choose Squarespace only if your buying job matches “Design-led website builder with commerce — Basic $16, Core $23, Plus $39, Advanced $99/mo ” rather than OpenCart's shape. Workflow advantage: OpenCart leans shared coverage; Squarespace leans checkout-conversion, website-builder-commerce. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — OpenCart and Squarespace share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: OpenCart is GPL open-source PHP cart — free download core; optional managed cloud cited ~$59–$99/mo by secondary sources (confirm live). WooCommerce kee; Squarespace is Design-led website builder with commerce — Basic $16, Core $23, Plus $39, Advanced $99/mo annual (US 2026 tiles); platform transaction fees .
- Company-size focus: OpenCart (small-business, mid-market) vs Squarespace (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: OpenCart-leaning — vs Squarespace-leaning checkout-conversion, website-builder-commerce.
- Researched limits: OpenCart — Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Squarespace — Platform transaction fees on lower tiers can exceed the subscription savings at volume.

Limitations — OpenCart: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0; Managed cloud floors are not first-party confirmed here — confirm live before budgeting; Squarespace: Platform transaction fees on lower tiers can exceed the subscription savings at volume; Catalog and B2B depth trail commerce-first platforms.

Poor-fit cases: OpenCart is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Hosting, security, and extension TCO are on you even when the license is $0 · Squarespace is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Platform transaction fees on lower tiers can exceed the subscription savings at volume · Avoid OpenCart if you actually need Squarespace's motion (Design-led website builder with commerce — Basic $16, Core $23, Plus $39, Advanc)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
